mcqs.q: A dental impression is best defined as:
opts: A negative imprint of the teeth and soft tissues from which a positive cast is formed
The positive stone model of the dental arch
A radiograph of the teeth and bone
A wax record of the patient's bite
mcqs.explain: The impression is the NEGATIVE imprint; the cast/model poured from it is the positive reproduction.
Alginate = irreversible hydrocolloid (elastic); agar = reversible hydrocolloid; ZOE/plaster/compound = non-elastic.

mcqs.q: Which is a NON-elastic impression material?
mcqs.explain: Non-elastic: zinc-oxide eugenol, impression compound, plaster. Alginate/agar are hydrocolloids; polyether is an elastomer.

mcqs.q: During setting, alginate (sodium/potassium alginate) reacts with calcium sulfate to form:
mcqs.explain: Alginate + calcium sulfate → insoluble calcium alginate gel.

mcqs.q: The ingredient added chiefly for strength and body in alginate is:
mcqs.explain: Diatomaceous earth provides strength/body; trisodium phosphate is the retarder.

mcqs.q: The role of trisodium phosphate in alginate is to:
opts: Act as a retarder, delaying gelation until it is consumed
mcqs.explain: The retarder reacts preferentially with calcium sulfate; when consumed, gel formation begins.

mcqs.q: Alginate impressions must be poured immediately because they undergo:
mcqs.explain: Water uptake (imbibition) and loss (syneresis) distort the impression, so pour immediately and keep at 100% humidity.

mcqs.q: The clinician can control alginate's setting time by adjusting the:
mcqs.explain: Higher water temperature speeds the set; lower slows it.

mcqs.q: Which tray feature does NOT provide mechanical retention of alginate?
mcqs.explain: Retention comes from rim locks, perforations, adhesive, or tray extension — not a smooth surface.

mcqs.q: An alginate impression should be removed from the mouth:
opts: Only after the stone has set
mcqs.explain: Remove with a quick snap 2–3 minutes after gelation to avoid tearing/distortion.

mcqs.q: A recommended method to disinfect an alginate impression is:
opts: Spray with glutaraldehyde and seal in a bag ~10 minutes
Leave it to dry in open air overnight
mcqs.explain: Spray glutaraldehyde, seal ~10 min, keep moist, then pour.

mcqs.q: For pouring a diagnostic cast, the recommended material and technique is:
opts: Vacuum-mixed ADA type-4 stone added in small amounts at one location with a vibrator
Fast-set plaster poured all at once
Impression compound melted into the tray
mcqs.explain: Add small increments of vacuum-mixed type-4 stone at one point, using a vibrator to minimize bubbles.

mcqs.q: Using a tray that is TOO SMALL for the arch typically causes:
opts: Soft-tissue displacement, distortion and tearing on removal
The material to stay unconfined over the palate
mcqs.explain: Too small → tissue displacement and distortion; solution is a correctly sized/modified tray.

mcqs.q: An air bubble trapped on an occlusal surface of the impression produces, on the cast, a:
mcqs.explain: A void in the impression casts as a positive nodule; check and carefully remove it.

opts: An accurate replication of the arch showing teeth and surrounding-tissue relationships
A negative imprint of the arch
mcqs.explain: The diagnostic cast is the positive replica used for analysis and planning.

mcqs.q: Which is a use of an articulated diagnostic cast in fixed prosthodontics?
opts: Rehearsing tooth preparations and performing a diagnostic wax-up
Replacing the need for any clinical exam
mcqs.explain: Uses: occlusal analysis, abutment evaluation, prep rehearsal, diagnostic wax-up (→ putty index), and custom-tray fabrication.

saqs.q: Define a dental impression and classify impression materials (with an example of each main group).
saqs.a: An impression is a negative imprint of the hard and soft tissues from which a positive cast is made. Non-elastic (rigid): ZOE, impression compound, plaster. Elastic — elastomers: polysulfide, silicone, polyether. Elastic — hydrocolloids: reversible (agar) and irreversible (alginate).

saqs.q: Describe the setting reaction of alginate and explain why the impression must be poured immediately.
saqs.a: Sodium/potassium alginate reacts with calcium sulfate to form insoluble calcium alginate (gel); trisodium phosphate acts as a retarder until consumed, then gelation begins. It must be poured immediately because imbibition (water uptake) and syneresis (water loss) distort the impression; store at 100% humidity.

saqs.q: List five guidelines for making a good alginate impression.
saqs.a: Use rigid, sturdy perforated/rim-lock trays; ensure teeth are clean (remove plaque, rinse, absorb saliva); make a uniform homogeneous mix; fill the tray sufficiently with no voids; ensure a good tray–material bond; and pour with cast material as soon as possible (store at 100% humidity, separate after 60 min).

saqs.q: Give three problems associated with alginate impressions and a solution for each.
saqs.a: 1) Tray too small → tissue displacement/distortion → use a suitable size or modify the tray. 2) Distortion from unsupported material/tray movement → extend the tray and modify its perimeter with modeling compound. 3) Air void → nodule on cast → check the cast and carefully remove nodules. (Also: sets too fast → adjust water temperature; over-dried teeth cause adhesion → don't over-dry.)

saqs.q: Define a diagnostic cast and list four of its uses in fixed prosthodontics.
saqs.a: A diagnostic cast is an accurate replication of the arch showing the relationships of teeth and surrounding tissues. Uses: analyze static/dynamic occlusion on an articulator; evaluate abutment alignment/angulation; rehearse tooth preparations; perform a diagnostic wax-up (and make a putty index); and fabricate a custom tray.
